Parent evidence track: #6
HIL decision task: #7

## Question this prototype answers

What does the product feel like when trying the Gitify-style reliability/inbox presentation versus the HeyClicky-style contextual presentation, using the exact experiment artifacts rather than static descriptions?

## Outcome

Create a clearly marked throwaway local comparison lab that a non-developer can start with one command.

The lab must provide three browser views:

1. side-by-side comparison and evidence gallery;
2. guided Gitify-style trial;
3. HeyClicky presentation-mode controls.

It must launch the exact packaged artifacts from:

- `feat/4-gitify-coaching-inbox`;
- `feat/5-heyclicky-presentation-modes`.

It must run only one `co.serp.KeylumeClone` experiment at a time, identify processes by exact executable path, and never terminate unrelated apps.

## Prototype boundary

- Throwaway pre-project evidence only.
- Branch directly from `origin/main`.
- Do not merge either experiment branch or copy their production source.
- Reference their committed screenshots and exact local packaged artifacts.
- No persistence, analytics, credentials, hosted deployment, or production integration.
- OpenClicky remains a future reference/HIL input; this lab does not install or run it.

## Required controls

- Show branch/commit/artifact availability.
- Launch Gitify-style app.
- Launch all HeyClicky modes or any individual mode.
- Stop the currently running exact experiment artifact.
- Link to issues, screenshot galleries, and Clipy motion evidence.
- Display concise guided steps for what the human should click/observe.
- Expose action/status output after every control.
- Support URL-switchable views and keyboard navigation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One documented command starts the localhost lab.
- [ ] Compare, Gitify, and HeyClicky views are URL-addressable.
- [ ] The exact artifact launcher is localhost-only and validates allowed paths.
- [ ] One experiment is stopped before another launches.
- [ ] Screenshot evidence is viewable directly in the dashboard.
- [ ] Each HeyClicky presentation mode can be launched individually.
- [ ] The Gitify guided flow explains how to create and review a test event.
- [ ] The prototype is visually verified in a browser.
- [ ] The branch, issue, and HIL task clearly state that this is pre-project evidence.
- [ ] No changes land on `main`.

comments.body: Live prototype is ready on branch codex/prototype-8-preproject-ui-comparison-lab at commit 577f9c6. From the prototype worktree, run: ./prototypes/preproject-ui-lab/run.sh. Then use http://127.0.0.1:8765/?variant=compare, variant=gitify, or variant=heyclicky. The lab provides side-by-side comparison, the full 19-image evidence galleries, a guided Gitify trial, deterministic controls for all six HeyClicky modes, and a localhost-only allowlisted launcher that keeps only one shared-bundle-ID experiment running at a time. Verified live: both pinned commits/artifacts match, all 19 PNG endpoints load, Gitify and HeyClicky launches both succeeded, switching stopped the previous experiment, tokenless mutation returned 403, and no experiment process was left running. This remains throwaway pre-project evidence and is not a merge recommendation; HIL selection remains tracked in #7.

Named native demo loop added on codex/prototype-8-preproject-ui-comparison-lab at commit 292fe99. From /Users/devin/dev/repos/clone-keylume-ios-app-ui-lab run ./scripts/dev-demo.sh baseline, gitify, or heyclicky. Generated bundles are visibly named Keylume Baseline Demo.app, Keylume Gitify Demo.app, and Keylume HeyClicky Demo.app; they live only under the prototype worktree and are never installed into /Applications. The runner stops the prior allowed demo, builds the selected worktree in debug mode, copies and re-signs the named bundle, launches it, reports its exact process path, supports xcode VARIANT/status/stop, and provides clean to remove only generated demo copies while preserving Swift caches. Live verification completed for all three universal builds, names, strict signatures, one-at-a-time switching, status, stop, and cleanup. No demo is currently running and main remains untouched.

body:
Parent: #6

## Human evaluation outcome

Compare OpenClicky and the HeyClicky-derived pre-project evidence side by side, then recommend which presentation concepts—if any—should inform a future shortcut-coaching product specification.

This is a **human-in-the-loop product decision**, not implementation authorization.

## Comparison sources

### OpenClicky

- [jasonkneen/openclicky](https://github.com/jasonkneen/openclicky)
- Public README, design notes, captures, and a local reference build only if it can be run without secrets/accounts.

### HeyClicky evidence

- #5 and its committed screenshot gallery
- [Feature-request recording](https://clipy.online/video/turp8hcj5pem)
- [Agent-readable recording context](https://clipy.online/video/turp8hcj5pem.md)
- [Six-mode V1 demo](https://clipy.online/video/kxpp3vf1uakl)
- Branch `feat/5-heyclicky-presentation-modes`

### Broader pre-project evidence

- #4 Gitify-style reliability/inbox experiment
- #2 notification/detection QA evidence

None of these is the selected production architecture or merge target.

## HIL procedure

1. Establish the exact OpenClicky commit/license/reference environment.
2. Review the OpenClicky UI evidence and run only safe UI flows that require no personal keys, accounts, local data access, microphone capture, or general agent execution.
3. Run the packaged HeyClicky-style showcase from #5.
4. Capture comparable screenshots at equivalent states and display geometry where practical.
5. Complete the decision matrix below.
6. Post a concise recommendation with selected, rejected, and unresolved patterns.
7. Obtain an explicit owner decision before opening any implementation issue.

## Decision matrix

Score each dimension from 1–5 and add concrete evidence:

| Pattern | OpenClicky | HeyClicky evidence | Preferred direction | Reason |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Menu-bar presence/status |  |  |  |  |
| Compact top-center status |  |  |  |  |
| Expanded coaching surface |  |  |  |  |
| Cursor opportunity cue |  |  |  |  |
| Pointer-anchored card/caption |  |  |  |  |
| Actionable decision banner |  |  |  |  |
| Multi-point guidance |  |  |  |  |
| Clear state transitions |  |  |  |  |
| Persistence/recoverability |  |  |  |  |
| Interruption level |  |  |  |  |
| Accessibility/Reduce Motion |  |  |  |  |
| Native macOS fit |  |  |  |  |

For each pattern choose one disposition:

- `select concept`;
- `combine concepts`;
- `adapt with original design`;
- `already covered`;
- `reject`;
- `out of scope`;
- `needs more evidence`.

## Guardrails

- Compare behavior and information hierarchy, not brand appeal alone.
- Do not copy exact visual styling, cursor artwork, sounds, words, animation timing, or trade dress.
- Do not treat MIT licensing as automatic approval to inherit product identity or architecture.
- Voice assistant, dictation, TTS, screen understanding, general agent execution, integrations, and account connectivity are out of scope unless separately authorized.
- Do not merge #4, #5, OpenClicky, or other reference code while completing this task.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Side-by-side screenshots/evidence are attached.
- [ ] Every matrix row is scored and has a disposition.
- [ ] Differences between observed behavior, documentation claims, and inference are identified.
- [ ] Accessibility, interruption cost, and recoverability are considered.
- [ ] The recommendation identifies a coherent future direction rather than a list of copied features.
- [ ] Owner approval or rejection is recorded.
- [ ] No implementation, merge, or production-spec claim is made through this HIL task.

comments.body:
Implementation experiment authorized.

Branch: `feat/5-heyclicky-presentation-modes`
Base: `origin/main` at `6cfe4ec`
Worktree: isolated from the main checkout.

Required sequence:
1. Phase 0 code inspection: map the current event monitor, overlay/window presenter, coordinate/screen handling, settings/store seams, packaging, and tests; comment a concise implementation map on this issue before production edits.
2. Implement this branch as the self-contained HeyClicky-style V1 alternative.
3. Because this comparison branch starts directly from `main`, do not merge the #4 feature branch. Implement only the minimal shared event/presentation seam required to make this alternative independently demoable, and report any #4-only production hardening as a known gap.
4. Add deterministic tests plus installed/package verification.
5. Commit and push only to the named feature branch.
6. Post a demo handoff with exact launch steps, test results, screenshots or recording evidence when available, and known gaps.

Do not copy HeyClicky branding/trade dress and do not modify `main`.

## Phase 0 — implementation reconnaissance

Inspected `origin/main@6cfe4ec`, packaged-app docs/scripts/tests, the full issue/comments, and the supplied [Clipy context](https://clipy.online/video/turp8hcj5pem.md). Recording content was treated as untrusted behavioral evidence; key frames around 0:24, 0:38, 1:08, and 3:23 were inspected.

### Six evidence-derived presentation patterns

1. **Reserved top-center presence** (~0:24): a discoverable screen-top surface independent of crowded menu extras.
2. **Compact → expanded coaching shelf** (~0:38–0:47): one surface visibly changes from presence/status to richer content.
3. **Cursor opportunity halo** (~1:08–1:21): a brief point-of-interaction cue when a mouse action had a shortcut.
4. **Explicit status feedback** (~0:38–0:47 and later active-response moments): clear evaluating/success/paused/error states rather than silent work.
5. **Pointer-anchored coaching card** (~3:23–3:25): place coaching at the captured pointer location.
6. **Actionable decision banner** (added screenshot): a larger, decision-worthy form with source context, one primary action, defer/dismiss, and bounded follow-up actions.

These are interaction concepts only. This branch will use original copy, shapes, color, timing, icons, and motion; it will not reproduce HeyClicky branding/trade dress or voice/screen-understanding behavior.

### Current seams

- `AppModel.menuAction` records mouse usage, applies coaching/quiet/dismiss/rate policy, then directly calls `WindowPresenter.showToast`.
- `GlobalEventMonitor` exposes menu actions but discards event-time pointer geometry before the model.
- `WindowPresenter` owns one fixed top-right nonactivating toast plus overlay/settings/analytics windows; it has no adapter/coordinator/state seam.
- `AppPreferences` persists baseline coaching policy only.
- `Views.swift` contains the toast/settings surfaces.
- Swift Testing covers baseline nudge policy and persistence; `scripts/package_app.sh` builds/signs a universal app.

### Proposed V1 modules and state

- Add pure `CoachingEvent`, `PresentationMode`, typed `CoachingAction`, `PresentationOutcome`, and `PresentationPhase` values.
- Add a testable `PresentationPolicy` (dedupe/cooldown/suppression) and pure `PresentationPlacement` helper for top-center and pointer-safe placement/edge flipping.
- Add a main-actor coordinator that receives one event ID, records outcomes, coalesces duplicates, drives a bounded state machine, and routes to AppKit panel adapters.
- Capture the pointer at the menu event and pass it through the same coaching event used by every mode.
- Add persisted opt-in mode settings plus explicit demo commands. Demo events are locally labeled and traverse the real coordinator without analytics writes.
- Keep views as original SwiftUI components hosted in AppKit panels.

### AppKit window and coordinate strategy

- One reusable borderless nonactivating `NSPanel` per transient role; halo panels are transparent, ignore mouse events, have no shadow, and never alter the system cursor.
- Event-time CG coordinates are converted into AppKit global coordinates against the screen containing the point; pure placement receives explicit display/visible frames so negative origins and edge flips are deterministic.
- Shelf uses the active/pointer screen visible frame and a reserved top inset; pointer cards avoid a hot-spot rectangle and clamp/flip within that screen.
- Panels join Spaces and are full-screen auxiliary for the demo, but tear down on screen-parameter/app termination notifications. No polling of screen content or pointer trails.
- Decision banner remains nonactivating; buttons use typed actions and are only interactive when the user deliberately enters the panel.

### Test and demo seams

- Deterministic tests: phase transitions/timeouts, duplicate suppression, cooldown/disabled/quiet suppression, pointer placement in corners/negative origins, top-center placement, typed action effects, fallback outcomes, and accessibility labels/action vocabulary.
- Demo path: menu-bar **Presentation Showcase** submenu with one trigger for each six modes and a **Run All Modes** sequence. This avoids depending on Chrome detection gaps from #2.
- Verification: `swift test`, completion validator, universal package/signing checks, exact packaged-app launch, then exercise demo triggers on the current Mac where permissions permit.

### Explicit comparison-branch gaps

This branch starts directly from `main` and will not merge #4. It will provide the minimal shared event/presentation seam and in-memory outcomes needed for an independent V1 demo, but it will **not** claim #4's durable Coaching History, unread menu/Dock/native-notification fan-out, crash recovery, or production-grade durable action/suppression audit. Events remain recoverable only through the baseline usage store, not a #4 history ledger. Full notch/auto-hide/remote-control/full-screen-video detection and interactive pointer-panel focus handoff are platform-hardening gaps unless safely proven in this slice.

Implementation begins after this comment.

## V1 comparison branch — demo-ready handoff

Implemented and pushed the isolated contextual-presentation alternative.

- Branch: `feat/5-heyclicky-presentation-modes`
- Commit: `8a1783f34c99ff548af775926388a2b82c566f93`
- Base remains `origin/main@6cfe4ec`; #4 was not merged.

### Build and launch the exact demo artifact

```sh
git fetch origin
git switch feat/5-heyclicky-presentation-modes
swift test
zsh scripts/package_app.sh release -
open -n .build/release/KeylumeClone.app --args --showcase=all
```

Launch one mode at a time with:

```sh
open -n .build/release/KeylumeClone.app --args --showcase=decisionBanner
```

Valid values: `topCenterPresence`, `compactExpandedShelf`, `cursorHalo`, `statusFeedback`, `pointerCard`, `decisionBanner`, and `all`.

The same triggers are available from the menu-bar **Presentation Showcase** submenu and Settings → Coaching. They use the real coordinator path, carry a shared preview event ID for a run, are visibly labeled local previews where appropriate, and do not add usage analytics.

### Verified packaged behavior

- Reserved top-center compact presence.
- Compact → expanded shelf transition.
- Transparent click-through cursor halo; low-motion behavior uses a static treatment.
- Evaluating → success status sequence with bounded teardown.
- Pointer card anchored to the event-time pointer and edge-aware placement.
- Wide decision banner with source context, one primary action, defer/dismiss, and bounded follow-up actions.
- Banner controls are exposed as native AX buttons. `Got It` was found as an `AXButton`, pressed through Accessibility, and dismissed the installed panel.
- Screen-parameter changes tear down presentation panels; previews never alter the system pointer or inspect/persist screen content or pointer trails.

Six-frame packaged-app proof:

- [Watch the demo](https://clipy.online/video/kxpp3vf1uakl)
- [Agent-readable demo context](https://clipy.online/video/kxpp3vf1uakl.md)

### Verification results

- `swift test`: **20 passed** (11 baseline + 9 new presentation tests).
- New deterministic coverage: state transitions, per-mode fan-out/dedupe, disabled/quiet/cooldown suppression, pointer placement in all corners and negative display origins, invalid placement, top-center display placement, typed action effects, accessible semantics/action ordering, and persisted presentation defaults.
- `python3 scripts/validate_completion.py`: **COMPLETE**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Static source/test/resource scan: no reference-product name, service, recording URL, or identifier.
- `scripts/package_app.sh release -`: passed; ad-hoc runtime signing verified; executable is universal `arm64` + `x86_64`.
- Exact artifact launched from `.build/release/KeylumeClone.app`; every mode produced a real on-screen AppKit panel in the packaged process.

### Known gaps / why this issue remains open

- This experiment intentionally does not contain #4's durable Coaching History, unread count, Dock/native notification fan-out, crash recovery, or durable delivery/action audit. In-memory presentation outcomes demonstrate the seam but are not production history.
- Installed visual proof was on the current built-in Retina display in dark appearance. Mixed-DPI/negative-origin placement is deterministic-test coverage only; notch, menu-bar auto-hide, display disconnect, Space changes, presentation/full-screen exclusions, Increase Contrast, Reduce Transparency, and VoiceOver reading order still need installed multi-configuration QA.
- `Stop Suggesting` persists through the existing dismissed-shortcut store; defer/read/action outcomes otherwise remain comparison-branch state until #4's durable model is integrated.
- Interactive pointer-panel focus handoff and keyboard traversal need broader installed testing beyond the successful AX button path.
- #2 still owns missed detection. Demo triggers intentionally avoid treating presentation success as detection reliability.
- Final visual defaults, brand assets/colors, animation policy, full-screen policy, and the criteria for the larger banner remain owner decisions.

This is ready for human side-by-side demo review, not issue closure.

## Late-reference clean-room delta audit

I reviewed the two public repositories added after the V1 handoff as behavioral/licensing evidence only. No code, assets, branding, copy, animation timing, or trade dress was incorporated.

### Evidence and provenance

- [`farzaa/clicky` at `a80fa807`](https://github.com/farzaa/clicky/tree/a80fa80721a8aebe51a170a7780705024ebc6e46) is MIT-licensed. Its [README](https://github.com/farzaa/clicky/blob/a80fa80721a8aebe51a170a7780705024ebc6e46/README.md) says the open-source repository remains available while newer work is private, so it is evidence for an older public Clicky implementation—not proof of current HeyClicky behavior.
- [`Bitshank-2338/clicky-windows` at `09208d8`](https://github.com/Bitshank-2338/clicky-windows/tree/09208d88740db7ba593eb6b95085b63e92a59772) is an MIT-licensed Windows/PyQt port. Its [README](https://github.com/Bitshank-2338/clicky-windows/blob/09208d88740db7ba593eb6b95085b63e92a59772/README.md) describes the same voice/screen-understanding cursor-companion concept on Windows.
- MIT availability does not change this issue's clean-room boundary. Since nothing was copied or derived from implementation source, no third-party notices or dependencies were added.

### Delta against the six V1 presentation patterns

| Issue #5 pattern | Late-reference observation | V1 delta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top-center presence | The public apps primarily use cursor-adjacent overlays plus a control panel/menu surface, not a new top-center coaching mode. | None. The original top-center shelf remains the intentional shortcut-coaching surface. |
| Compact → expanded shelf | The repos show control-panel and response-bubble state changes, but no additional shortcut-specific compact/expanded transition. | None. V1 already demonstrates the required two-stage shelf transition. |
| Cursor opportunity halo | Both repos use a continuously cursor-following companion; listening/processing/responding can morph its glyph, and the Windows port also describes cursor flight/pointing. | No in-scope gap. V1's original opportunity ring plus status cue communicates presence without replacing or continuously chasing the system pointer. |
| Explicit status feedback | The public implementations use text, color, waveform/spinner/triangle state changes for idle/listening/processing/responding. | No new state category for this product. V1 already uses icon, shape, color, and text rather than color alone. Paused/permission/error installed behavior remains production hardening already recorded in the prior handoff, not a newly revealed presentation mode. |
| Pointer-anchored card | The macOS response overlay follows the *live* pointer and flips/clamps near screen edges. | None—and intentionally different. Issue #5 requires event-time anchoring so the card does not chase the user's cursor; V1 implements event-time placement plus edge flip/clamp and deterministic tests. |
| Actionable decision banner | Neither public repo shows a comparable durable shortcut-decision hierarchy. Their core interaction is voice/chat response and screen guidance. | None. The issue screenshot/recording remains the relevant evidence, and V1 already includes primary, secondary, and dismiss actions. |

### Explicitly excluded behaviors

The following observed behaviors belong to a voice/screen-understanding cursor assistant and are outside this issue's stated scope: a permanently following custom cursor buddy; replacing the cursor cue with waveform/spinner glyphs; cursor flight, trails, or target navigation; screen capture and target detection; speech/streaming responses; and whiteboard/arrow/circle annotations. The Windows implementation's taskbar-specific overlay gap is platform-specific and irrelevant to macOS.

### Result

These references reinforce the existing mapping—cursor-adjacent presence, explicit processing state, edge-aware placement, and non-focus-stealing overlays—but reveal **no concrete missing in-scope presentation behavior** beyond the six modes already implemented. Adding their distinctive cursor-assistant behaviors would contradict the issue's clean-room and “do not implement a voice assistant/screen-understanding product” constraints.

Therefore I made **no code change**. The demo branch remains `feat/5-heyclicky-presentation-modes` at commit [`8a1783f`](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/commit/8a1783f34c99ff548af775926388a2b82c566f93), with the previously reported 20-test and packaged-demo verification unchanged.

## Exact packaged UI screenshot gallery

Gallery commit: [`ec844dc`](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/commit/ec844dc)

Full requirement map and capture notes: [`docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/README.md`](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/README.md)

The issue #4 worktree build and the `/Applications` copy sharing `co.serp.KeylumeClone` were resolved by executable path and stopped before capture. Every image below is from the rebuilt, universal, ad-hoc-signed issue #5 package at `.build/release/KeylumeClone.app`; crops contain only app-owned UI.

### 1. Reserved top-center / compact shelf

![Exact packaged top-center compact presence](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/01-top-center-compact-presence.png?raw=true)

### 2. Expanded coaching shelf/card

![Exact packaged expanded coaching shelf](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/02-expanded-coaching-shelf.png?raw=true)

### 3. Cursor opportunity halo

![Exact packaged cursor opportunity halo](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/03-cursor-opportunity-halo.png?raw=true)

### 4. Pointer-anchored coaching card

![Exact packaged pointer-anchored coaching card](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/04-pointer-anchored-coaching-card.png?raw=true)

### 5. Near-edge placement flips to the safe side

The pointer is visible below/right of the card; the surface remains inside the display rather than covering or overflowing the event point.

![Exact packaged pointer card edge-flip placement](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/05-pointer-card-edge-flip.png?raw=true)

### 6. Explicit status — evaluating

![Exact packaged evaluating status](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/06-status-evaluating.png?raw=true)

### 7. Explicit status — success

![Exact packaged success status](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/07-status-success.png?raw=true)

### 8. Actionable decision banner

This shows the primary `Practice Shortcut`, defer `Not Now`, dismiss `Got It`, `Coaching Settings`, and `Stop Suggesting This Shortcut` actions, plus the shortcut and local-preview chips.

![Exact packaged actionable decision banner](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/08-actionable-decision-banner.png?raw=true)

### 9. Settings controls and real presentation previews

All six mode switches, per-mode Preview controls, Run All, and reset defaults are visible.

![Exact packaged presentation settings](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/09-settings-presentation-controls.png?raw=true)

### Screenshot-review bug fixed

The capture pass found a real lifecycle defect: the expanded shelf reached its expanded frame and immediately disappeared because scheduling dismissal canceled the active transition task. Commit `ec844dc` separates transition and dismissal task slots and adds `presentationDismissalDoesNotCancelActiveStateTransition` regression coverage. The rebuilt package now holds the expanded state for its intended duration.

### Verification

- `swift test`: **21 tests passed**
- `zsh scripts/package_app.sh release -`: **passed**
- `codesign --verify --deep --strict`: **passed**
- packaged executable: **universal x86_64 + arm64**
- existing motion demo: [Clipy video](https://clipy.online/video/kxpp3vf1uakl) / [agent-readable context](https://clipy.online/video/kxpp3vf1uakl.md)

### Coverage and explicit gaps

- Covered by exact stills: compact top-center, expanded shelf, halo, pointer card, edge flip, evaluating, success, actionable banner/action hierarchy, and all Settings preview controls.
- Compact→expanded and evaluating→success timing require motion evidence; the paired endpoints above plus the Clipy recording cover those transitions.
- Reduce Motion is implemented through the live macOS setting: it removes top-panel frame animation and uses a static halo diameter. The final still is intentionally equivalent, so no duplicate still is claimed as separate proof.
- `paused`, permission-required, and failed phases exist in the bounded state/semantic model, but this packaged visual showcase visibly implements only evaluating and success; no unshipped visual state is represented here.
- The menu-bar extra's exact AX hierarchy contains `Presentation Showcase`, all six individual triggers, `Run All Six Modes`, and `Hide Showcase`: [AX evidence](https://github.com/serpcompany/keylume-mac-hotkey-app-clone/blob/ec844dc/docs/evidence/issue-5-presentation-gallery/menu-bar-showcase-ax.txt). macOS culled the icon behind the current crowded/notched menu bar, so a clean menu still was not possible without changing unrelated apps or the user's persistent menu layout.
- Button side effects, dedupe/suppression, action ordering, accessibility semantics, and placement bounds remain deterministic test evidence rather than still-image claims.

The issue remains open and `ready-for-human` for side-by-side product review.

title: Add HeyClicky-inspired contextual presentation modes for shortcut coaching

comments.body: Follow-up presentation-layer issue created: #5. It depends on this issue's durable event/history pipeline and shared event ID; #5 must not introduce a parallel source of truth.

Implementation experiment authorized.

Branch: `feat/4-gitify-coaching-inbox`
Base: `origin/main` at `6cfe4ec`
Worktree: isolated from the main checkout.

Required sequence:
1. Phase 0 code inspection: map the current event monitor, toast/window presenter, settings/store seams, packaging, and tests; comment a concise implementation map on this issue before production edits.
2. Implement this branch as the self-contained Gitify-style V1 alternative.
3. Add deterministic tests plus installed/package verification.
4. Commit and push only to the named feature branch.
5. Post a demo handoff with exact launch steps, test results, screenshots or recording evidence when available, and known gaps.

Do not copy Gitify branding/trade dress and do not modify `main`.

## Phase 0 implementation reconnaissance

### Current seams

- `GlobalEventMonitor.onMenuAction` → `AppModel.menuAction` is the only characterized eligible coaching-opportunity path. Keyboard usage is analytics only; Chrome/action detection gaps remain owned by #2.
- `AppModel` currently applies cooldown/quiet/dismissal policy and calls `WindowPresenter.showToast` directly. The toast has no outcome record.
- `UsageStore` is an actor-backed local JSON pattern that can be mirrored for a versioned coaching-history envelope. `AppPreferences` is the existing local settings seam.
- `MenuBarExtra` is currently a static menu-style extra; `WindowPresenter` owns all AppKit windows/panels.
- Packaging is SwiftPM → `scripts/package_app.sh` → ad-hoc/supplied signing. `Resources/Info.plist` currently has `LSUIElement=true`; the packaged app is therefore accessory-only.
- Tests are Swift Testing with injectable `UserDefaults` and store URLs. No installed E2E harness from #2 exists on this branch.

### Proposed modules and data flow

1. Add a versioned `CoachingEvent` domain record and actor-backed `CoachingHistoryStore` with atomic JSON persistence, UUID idempotency, 500-item/30-day retention, and migration coverage.
2. Persist the event before any presentation. Keep one event ID while independently updating toast/native/Dock delivery outcomes.
3. Add pure `CoachingPresentationPolicy` and `DockAttentionPolicy` seams for deterministic clock/rate-limit tests.
4. Extend `AppModel` as the single observable source for history/unread state and mutations (seen/unseen, permanent dismissal/restore, clear, test event).
5. Replace the static menu with an original native window-style popover showing recent events/count/Mark All Seen/Open History.
6. Add an original native Coaching History window with search/filter/review and a Notification & Attention settings section.
7. Add AppKit adapters for Dock badge/informational attention and optional UserNotifications delivery/deep-linking. Change the demo identity to regular Dock activation and `LSUIElement=false`.

### Test seams

- Store load/append/idempotency/retention/schema-v1 migration and corruption reporting.
- Shared unread count across add/seen/unseen/dismiss/clear/reload.
- Structured toast suppression outcomes and bounce eligibility/rate limiting.
- Notification request construction/deduplication at the adapter boundary; OS banner visibility itself remains an installed/manual observation.
- Existing analytics/preferences/event-tap tests stay green.

### Demo path

Package `.build/release/KeylumeClone.app`, launch it, use **Send Test Coaching Event** (does not write usage analytics), then compare the custom toast, green numbered menu-bar popover, persistent Coaching History, optional native notification, Dock badge, and bounded informational bounce. Relaunch to prove restoration.

### Safe V1 boundary / known limits

This branch will not claim #2's missing Chrome New Tab/tab-strip detection is fixed. Focus/scheduled-delivery cannot be observed as a visible banner through `UNUserNotificationCenter`; the event will distinguish submitted-to-system from visible delivery. Exact live Notification Center presentation, login-item launch, multiple Spaces/full-screen, and Accessibility-driven app journeys require installed human/E2E proof after deterministic tests and package launch. No Gitify assets, copy, exact layout, or trade dress will be used.

## Demo-ready implementation handoff

Implemented and pushed the isolated Gitify-style V1 experiment.

- Branch: `feat/4-gitify-coaching-inbox`
- Commit: `ae3e8aea93f1322e898cbe39f12763b11a405149` (short: `ae3e8ae`)
- Base: `origin/main` at `6cfe4ec`

### What is working

- A versioned, local, actor-backed coaching history is persisted before any transient presentation.
- Stable event IDs, idempotent append, atomic writes, v1 legacy-array migration, 500-item/30-day retention, and relaunch restoration.
- Structured toast outcomes for shown, cooldown, hourly-cap, quiet-hours, disabled, excluded-app, and dismissed-shortcut cases.
- Original window-style menu-bar inbox with recent events, exact unread count, Mark All Seen, original green unread icon, and distinct orange permission/history-error state.
- Persistent native Coaching History with newest-first list, unread/dismissed/application filters, action/shortcut search, delivery outcome, seen/unseen, permanent shortcut dismissal/restore, clear confirmation, empty/error states, and accessibility labels.
- Regular Dock identity (`LSUIElement=false`), original code-drawn app icon, shared system Dock badge, Dock reopen to the singleton history window, and bounded informational attention policy.
- Optional permission-aware UserNotifications delivery with one event ID and exact-item activation callback. Delivery records `submitted-to-system` without claiming a visible banner.
- Independent notification sound/volume, menu count/highlight, Dock badge/bounce, and toast settings.
- **Send Test Coaching Event** exercises presentation without writing fake usage analytics.

### Exact demo

git switch feat/4-gitify-coaching-inbox
swift test
zsh scripts/package_app.sh release -
open .build/release/KeylumeClone.app

## Outcome

Create a living, automation-oriented QA inventory for shortcut coaching reliability, then exercise the installed reference and candidate apps to identify missing, intermittent, duplicate, or incorrect coaching behavior—starting with Google Chrome.

In this issue, **notification** means the app's in-product coaching toast shown after a pointer-driven action that has a discoverable keyboard shortcut. Distinguish it from macOS Notification Center notifications.

This is a QA discovery and test-planning issue. Do not fix implementation behavior, redesign UI, rename/rebrand the app, alter the frozen Goal 1 evidence, or implement Goal 2 UI.

## User-reported seed failures

1. **Chrome menu action:** pointer-click Chrome `File → New Tab` (`⌘T`) → no coaching toast observed, but one is expected.
2. **Chrome control case:** pointer-click Chrome `File → New Window` (`⌘N`) → coaching toast appears.
3. **Chrome tab-strip action:** while viewing one tab, pointer-click the immediately adjacent tab → no coaching toast observed; desired product behavior is a suggestion such as `⌃Tab` for next tab.

Do not assume case 3 is already reference behavior. Compare the installed Keylume reference and candidate:

- candidate differs from reference → parity defect;
- both omit it but the desired behavior is technically supportable → product enhancement candidate;
- behavior cannot be mapped reliably to one shortcut → unresolved product/technical decision.

## User-supplied source material

A local Notion export named `Hotkeys` is available to the assigned agent. It includes a keyboard-symbol catalog and a shortcut cheatsheet. Do not commit the raw archive or private Notion metadata.

Normalize relevant cases from it, but treat live application menus and observed macOS behavior as the authority. The export may contain stale, app-specific, or incorrect mappings.

Initial browser/system seeds include:

- Open new window — `⌘N`
- Open new tab — `⌘T`
- Reopen closed tab — `⇧⌘T`
- Close tab/window — `⌘W`
- Focus address bar — `⌘L`
- Next tab — `⌃Tab`
- Previous tab — verify the live Chrome shortcut rather than trusting the export
- Navigate to numbered tab — `⌘1` through `⌘9`, where Chrome exposes them
- Find/find next/find previous
- Back navigation

## Required workflow

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/*`, `docs/app-replica/scope.md`, `parity-ledger.md`, `verification.md`, and the existing tests.
2. Use the `clean-room-native-app-replica` and `diagnosing-bugs` skills.
3. Use Computer Use for live Chrome/reference/candidate actions when available. Prefer AX-indexed actions; use coordinates only when Chrome's tab strip or native menu is not exposed adequately.
4. Preserve the accepted installed candidate and reference artifacts. Record their bundle/version/hash identity before trials.
5. Establish a repeatable state reset before judging a case:
   - Accessibility granted;
   - coaching enabled;
   - Chrome not excluded;
   - quiet hours inactive;
   - dismissed-shortcut state understood/reset or isolated;
   - rate-limit/minimum-interval/hourly-cap state understood;
   - reference/candidate analytics and preference contamination avoided or explicitly recorded.
6. Run each P0 seed repeatedly—target 10 trials per app/action after reset—to measure intermittent behavior instead of recording a single anecdote.
7. Capture enough evidence to distinguish event capture, menu-item resolution, shortcut matching, notification-policy suppression, and toast presentation.
8. Do not add broad logging. If temporary instrumentation becomes necessary, stop and put the exact proposed instrumentation in the owner-decision queue; do not change production code in this issue.

## Living deliverables

Create:

- `docs/qa/coaching-notification-matrix.md` — human-readable running QA list, findings, missing coverage, and prioritized automation backlog.
- `docs/qa/coaching-notification-cases.json` — machine-readable cases suitable for later test generation.

Each case must include:

- stable case ID;
- application and version;
- action and UI surface (`menu-bar`, `tab-strip`, `toolbar`, `context-menu`, `overlay`, or `keyboard`);
- live-observed shortcut;
- preconditions/reset requirements;
- exact action steps;
- expected reference behavior;
- expected candidate/product behavior;
- reference results and candidate results with trial counts;
- classification (`pass`, `parity-defect`, `intermittent`, `product-enhancement`, `unsupported`, or `blocked`);
- likely automation layer (`unit`, `integration`, `installed-e2e`, or `human-only`);
- evidence path;
- follow-up issue needed;
- status and last-verified date.

## Minimum test dimensions

### Event source

- Native menu-bar pointer click
- App toolbar/control pointer click when it maps to a menu shortcut
- Chrome tab-strip click
- Context-menu selection
- Keyboard invocation as a negative coaching control
- Candidate overlay execution as a keyboard-usage control

### Policy and state

- First eligible mouse action
- Repeated same action inside/outside cooldown
- Different eligible action during cooldown
- Permanently dismissed shortcut
- Dismissal reset
- Coaching disabled
- Quiet hours
- Hourly cap/rate limit
- Excluded application
- Accessibility unavailable/revoked
- Relaunch persistence

### Toast correctness

- Appears when eligible
- Does not appear for keyboard use or shortcutless actions
- Correct action title and shortcut glyph/order
- Correct foreground application
- No duplicate or stale toast
- Expected timing, position, dismissal, and close/permanent-dismiss behavior

### Cross-application smoke coverage

After Chrome P0 cases, seed at least Finder and one additional installed app with live AX menu shortcuts. Clearly separate executed cases from backlog-only cases.

## Automation backlog requirements

For every missing test, name the narrowest real seam and a red-capable assertion. Prioritize:

- **P0:** reproduces a user-observed failure or flaky notification path;
- **P1:** policy/reset/persistence and installed integration coverage;
- **P2:** broader shortcut/app compatibility and presentation details.

Do not claim a unit test covers a real menu-pointer flow when only an installed-app E2E can exercise it. If no deterministic seam exists, document the missing seam and propose the smallest harness needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both reported Chrome menu cases are exercised on the reference and candidate with repeated trials.
- [ ] The Chrome adjacent-tab click is exercised and classified as parity defect, enhancement, unsupported, or blocked based on evidence.
- [ ] Rate limiting, dismissed state, quiet hours, exclusions, and permission state are ruled in/out as causes of missing toasts.
- [ ] The normalized source-material cases are represented in the running backlog without committing the raw export.
- [ ] Human and JSON QA inventories exist and validate.
- [ ] Every executed case includes trial counts and evidence; backlog-only cases are labeled as such.
- [ ] Missing automated coverage is prioritized P0/P1/P2 with the correct test seam.
- [ ] No implementation fix, Goal 1 rewrite, rebrand, or Goal 2 UI work is performed.
- [ ] Existing tests/build remain green.

## Handoff

Comment on this issue with:

1. reproduced failures and rates;
2. reference-versus-candidate differences;
3. policy/state causes ruled in or out;
4. top P0 automated tests to implement next;
5. blockers and owner decisions;
6. validation commands and exact changed files.

Leave the issue open and move it to `ready-for-human` after the QA audit is complete. Separate implementation/fix tickets should be created only after owner review.

## Outcome

This is an **audit-only** issue. Do not rename the app, redesign UI, replace assets, change behavior, or implement the Goal 2 management UI.

## Required workflow

1. Read `AGENTS.md` and the configured docs under `docs/agents/`.
2. Use the `clean-room-native-app-replica` skill at `/Users/devin/.agents/skills/clean-room-native-app-replica/SKILL.md`.

Leave replacement and owner-decision values unresolved when they require product, creative, licensing, or legal judgment. Do not invent those decisions.

- Tooltips, menus, About, onboarding, settings, alerts, errors, empty states, notifications, permission prompts, accessibility labels, Finder/Dock surfaces, and packaged documents.

- Fonts, libraries, images, sounds, datasets, models, and other third-party dependencies, including license and attribution requirements.

## Independence proof

Establish whether the candidate has any dependency on Keylume services, identifiers, accounts, or update infrastructure:

- Search source, config, tests, docs, build products, strings, assets, metadata, and release artifacts for Keylume names, domains, identifiers, and known endpoints.
- Build/package if safe and inspect the resulting `.app` without changing the installed accepted artifact.
- Exercise network-capable paths using non-secret configuration and record destinations. Classify each as candidate-owned, Apple/platform-owned, approved third party, reference-owned, or unresolved.
- Identify identity-sensitive persistence and OS integration paths that must be retested after rebranding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every discovered item appears in both the human inventory and machine-readable manifest.
- [ ] Original name, logo, icons, artwork, sounds, copy, and reference-derived design values are explicitly covered.
- [ ] Every service, identifier, account, credential boundary, and update mechanism is explicitly covered.
- [ ] Static source/config/docs evidence is included.
- [ ] Packaged-artifact evidence is included, or the exact safe blocker is documented.
- [ ] Runtime/network evidence is included for every network-capable path, or the exact safe blocker is documented.
- [ ] No secrets or private reference data are copied, printed, or committed.
- [ ] No rebrand implementation or Goal 2 UI work is performed.
- [ ] All unresolved product/legal/creative decisions are grouped into a concise owner-decision queue.

1. audit result and counts by disposition/category;
